long_biography.plain_text:
At Adamas, investment manager Barry Lau narrowed a lending business that had ranged from India to Australasia. Monitoring companies across different time zones and cultures had proved cumbersome, so he concentrated on Greater China and loans with stronger repayment priority. He sought growing businesses whose founders wanted expansion capital without selling equity.

His team also intervened in how borrowers were run. When one founder's management style hindered staff, Adamas helped move him into the chairmanship and brought in a chief executive. Other safeguards included placing financial controllers inside borrower companies, joining their boards and sharing control of bank accounts.
